## Overview

Add bounded tool-calling metrics for Chat Completions and Messages, covering streaming and non-streaming responses without changing parser behavior or model output.

## Claims

- Add `vllm:tool_call_responses_total` (`model_name`, `status`) and `vllm:tool_calls_emitted_total` (`model_name`), counting returned calls after filtering and Messages conversion without double-counting streaming fragments. Existing parser-counter labels and classifications remain unchanged.
- Add `vllm:request_tools`, a histogram observed once per request before parsing, including requests without tools.

## Validation

369 focused tests passed: 39 parser/metrics and 330 Chat/Messages serving tests. All applicable pre-commit checks passed. Existing Buildkite jobs cover these suites.
<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/parser/test_tool_calling_metrics.py \
  tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/parser -q --tb=short -x

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints \
  -k 'not test_serving_chat or full_tool_response or stream_tool_response or chat_per_request_metrics or streaming_reasoning_usage or streaming_logprobs_kept or test_resolve_finish_reason or empty or abort or streaming_chunks or streaming_error' \
  -q --tb=short -x
```

--confcutdir excludes the global accelerator-cleanup fixture, which crashes in the local macOS PyTorch environment. The fixture is unchanged.
</details>

Earlier live validation of the metrics-only revision (`f9798f7e27`): 24/24 CPU cases passed on ROSA with Qwen3-0.6B and tracing disabled. Verified 20 tool-bearing response outcomes, 14 emitted calls, and four plain-request controls with no new counter increments. Streaming `n=2` counted one outcome and two calls; the legacy counter retained its schema and Messages attribution. This used the exact Python source over the existing CPU image's native libraries, not a rebuilt candidate image. The revised labels and new histogram passed an in-process HTTP `/metrics` smoke test; live-model validation of those changes is still pending. A non-tool performance comparison remains pending. No end-to-end performance claim is made.

## Details

Tracing is handled separately in [#62109](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62109), keeping this PR focused on metrics.

The new telemetry exports no tool names, schemas, arguments, bodies, or content-derived hashes. Failures cover surfaced exceptions only; internally swallowed errors and existing payload logging remain outside this PR.

This differs from [#51814](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51814) and [#53365](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53365), which cover invocation tests/hooks, and [#54117](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54117)/[#55254](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55254), which classify parser completions against schemas. This PR measures actual API response outcomes after filtering/conversion.

+## Tool-calling Metrics
+
+Tool-calling metrics cover parsing model output, recording request outcomes,
+and returning tool calls to the client. These counters measure different units,
+so their totals need not match. All three include `model_name`.
+
+| Counter | What it counts |
+| --- | --- |
+| `vllm:tool_call_parser_invocations_total` | Each parser invocation: once per choice for non-streaming output, or per output fragment when streaming. Only parsers using the recording hook are counted. |
+| `vllm:tool_call_responses_total` | One outcome per completed request with tools, or per surfaced parsing failure. |
+| `vllm:tool_calls_emitted_total` | Individual tool-call objects returned after filtering and response conversion. |
+
+For example, a streaming request produces two tool calls after 20 parser
+invocations. The parser counter increases by 20, the response counter by one
+with `status="success"`, and the emitted-call counter by two. Later argument
+fragments for the same call do not add calls. These metrics count instructions
+returned to the client, not executions of those instructions.
+
+The response counter's only additional label is `status`:
+
+- `success`: a completed response contains tool calls.
+- `no_tool_calls`: a completed response contains no tool calls.
+- `parse_failure`: the combined reasoning/tool parser raises an exception,
+  or non-streaming Messages tool arguments fail conversion.
+
+A failed non-streaming response emits zero calls. Interrupted streams retain
+already-emitted calls without recording a completed outcome. Generic engine
+errors and cancellation are not classified as parsing failures. Streaming
+argument JSON is not validated, so `success` does not guarantee valid or complete
+arguments. Errors caught internally by parsers cannot be distinguished from
+ordinary output.
+
+`vllm:request_tools` is a separate histogram of supplied tool definitions.
+Its only application label is `model_name`, with bucket boundaries `0`, `1`,
+`5`, `10`, and `+Inf`. Each validated request reaching the shared Chat/Messages
+handler is observed once before parsing, including requests without tools.
+Streaming fragments, response choices, and Messages conversion do not add
+observations.
+
+The response counters cover Chat Completions and Messages requests with tools.
+Cohere v2 also uses the Chat handler and is counted before Cohere response
+conversion. Requests without tools skip these counters but contribute zero to
+the request histogram.
+
+The existing parser counter is unchanged. Its labels are `mode` (`streaming`
+or `non_streaming`), `outcome` (`tool_call` or `no_tool_call`), and `request_type`
+(`chat_completions`, `responses`, or `other`). Messages requests are converted
+to Chat requests before parsing, so their `request_type` is `chat_completions`.
+Exceptions remain `no_tool_call` on this counter; the response counter reports
+surfaced parsing failures separately.
+
+The new metrics contain no tool names, schemas, arguments, request bodies,
+or content-derived hashes. Existing application logging is separate.
+

I find this pretty impenetrable, given this is user-facing. Before getting into the semantics of the labels, I'd open with something like

---

Tool-calling metrics describe three parts of handling a request: parsing model output, recording the request's outcome, and returning individual tool calls to the client.

These counters measure different units, so their totals need not match. All three include the `model_name` label.

| Counter | What it counts |
|---|---|
| `vllm:tool_call_parser_invocations_total` | Each time the tool parser examines model output. Streaming can require many invocations for one request. |
| `vllm:tool_call_responses_total` | One outcome per completed tool-bearing request, or per surfaced parsing failure. |
| `vllm:tool_calls_emitted_total` | Individual tool-call objects returned to the client. One response can contain several calls. |

For example, a streamed request asks for weather in two cities. The parser examines 20 output fragments, and the completed response contains two `get_weather` calls:

- Parser invocations increase by **20**.
- Response outcomes increase by **1**, with `status="success"`.
- Emitted tool calls increase by **2**.

Fragments extending an existing call's arguments do not count as additional calls. Emitted calls are instructions for the client application to execute; these metrics do not measure tool execution.

Streaming calls can be emitted before the response finishes. Some tool-calling paths bypass the parser recording hook, so this is a conceptual relationship rather than a fixed counting ratio.

Thanks for pushing on our observability! I went through some human and AI-assisted review with this, and found a few things we should probably adjust before merging this. Items 1 and 2 are the bigger ones; 3–4 are small and can go in the same push. Reviewed at 5f74a0c.

I did not mark these as request changes, because I know others have been tagged for review and am leaving room for them to push back or override my suggestions below.

**1. Every Chat output now pays for a pydantic private-attribute read**

[`serving.py#L557`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f74a0c080c04468aefc3d34c4a1a680a47f9079/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py#L557) and [`#L1025`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f74a0c080c04468aefc3d34c4a1a680a47f9079/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py#L1025) read `request._tool_calling_spans` on every `RequestOutput`, for every Chat request, including ones with no tools and tracing off. Pydantic private attributes are resolved through `BaseModel.__getattr__`, so each read costs about 670 ns, against about 11 ns for a normal field (pydantic 2.14). I benchmarked `chat_completion_stream_generator` on CPU, feeding it 1,000 mocked outputs with no tools and no tracing. Median time went from 12.19 ms on base to 13.12 ms on this PR, and back to 12.14 ms with the read moved out of the loop. This isn't an end-to-end number, but it's a cost on the hot path for a feature most requests don't use. Please read it once before each loop using something like:

```python
tool_calling_spans = request._tool_calling_spans
async for res in result_generator:
    if tool_calling_spans is not None:
        tool_calling_spans.extend(res._tool_calling_spans or ())
        res._tool_calling_spans = None
```

**2. Don't change the labels on `vllm:tool_call_parser_invocations_total` unless we deprecate/migrate first**

This counter has shipped since v0.24.0 (#44448) with labels `model_name, mode, outcome, request_type`. This PR moves Messages traffic from `request_type="chat_completions"` to `"messages"` and adds `tool_choice` and `tool_count` ([`metrics.py#L236-L260`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f74a0c080c04468aefc3d34c4a1a680a47f9079/vllm/parser/metrics.py#L236-L260)). Dashboards and alerts that select `request_type="chat_completions"` would silently lose Messages traffic after an upgrade. The new `vllm:tool_call_responses_total` already has `tool_choice` and `api_surface`, so could we leave the existing counter as it is and put the new dimensions on the new counters (including `tool_count`, if you want it)? If you'd rather change the existing counter, it needs an explicit deprecation and migration note, but I think leaving it alone is the faster way to land this. What I want to avoid is surprising people with production deployments on upgrades.

**3. Errors from the new close calls escape the stream's `finally`**

At [`serving.py#L981`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f74a0c080c04468aefc3d34c4a1a680a47f9079/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py#L981) and [`anthropic/serving.py#L1277`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f74a0c080c04468aefc3d34c4a1a680a47f9079/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py#L1277), if `aclose()` raises (for example, the engine abort fails while the generator closes), the exception escapes after the error chunk has been yielded. Chat never sends `[DONE]`, and the Messages stream breaks. This can only happen with tracing on and tools present, because that's the only case where Chat closes the engine generator. Still, it's a new failure mode on the error path. Please wrap both calls in `try/except Exception: logger.exception(...)` so cleanup failures get logged instead of raised.

**4. A few accuracy fixes in `docs/usage/metrics.md`**

- [L61](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f74a0c080c04468aefc3d34c4a1a680a47f9079/docs/usage/metrics.md?plain=1#L61) says Messages argument-conversion errors count as parse failures. That's only true for non-streaming. Streaming forwards argument fragments without validating them, so invalid or truncated JSON is recorded as `success`. Qualifying the sentence is fine for this PR.
- Cohere v2 calls `create_chat_completion` without setting `_api_surface`, so its traffic is counted as `chat_completions`, before the Cohere conversion. Please mention that in one sentence, or exclude Cohere explicitly.
- On a request with tools, an exception from the combined parser, including the reasoning parser, is recorded as `parse_failure`. That's a reasonable signal, but the table describes it as a tool-parser failure, so please say this explicitly.

One additional note as I dug into the labels themselves - consider keeping `tool_choice` and `tool_count` off `tool_call_parser_invocations_total` regardless of how `request_type` is handled. That counter goes up once per streamed chunk, so a single streamed request that produces 300 chunks adds 300, while a non-streamed request adds 1. That makes it hard to answer questions like "how many requests set `tool_choice=required`?" from it. Since these describe the request, they fit better on `tool_call_responses_total`, which counts each request once.

The cardinality of the new labels isn't a concern either way, but keeping the old counter's labels unchanged also keeps it around I believe 18 series instead of potentially as high as 720 with this change as-is.

I'm not a maintainer of the serving layer, but I'm struggling to get comfortable with the way the collection of these tool calling metrics are scattered across the request handling path. In particular, the way we defer the metric recording just for the anthropic layer because further parsing can happen later in that serving layer ... it's just too much of a hack that takes us down a difficult to extend and maintain path IMO

I spent some time exploring options, and what looked least-worse (to me) is a `ToolCallingStats` object attached to the request object. We'd accumulate the various counters and error conditions there, and only when the request is complete actually record to Prometheus. This allows us to do things like have a late parsing failure invalidate the counters recorded earlier.

Feel free to push back if you don't agree with the direction, it's just my idea

Oh, also - I'm definitely unsure about recording multiple, parallel-sampled response choices as a single response

<details>
<summary>Detailed agent instructions</summary>

Currently, metrics are exported while parsing and conversion are still in progress. Anthropic can fail decoding tool arguments after shared Chat processing succeeds, and streaming adapters may emit different tool events from shared raw chunks. Replace scattered observations with request-scoped accumulation and one final export.

Follow these principles:

1.  Distinguish the measurement units. Parser metrics count invocations; emitted-call metrics count individual tool calls; response-outcome metrics should count individual sampled choices, including choices produced by parallel sampling. For a successful request with three choices, two containing tool calls, record two success outcomes and one no_tool_calls outcome. Several calls within one choice contribute one response outcome. Observe the supplied-tool histogram once per request. 
2. Accumulate facts before observing metrics. Add ToolCallStats in vllm/parser/metrics.py. Capture supplied tool count, parser invocation counters, model label, and per-choice response counts, emitted-call identities, completion, and failure state. Later layers can override provisional counts. Parsing failures remain sticky for affected choices. Attribute failures to individual choices when possible; request-wide failures must prevent false successes. Make final observation idempotent.
3. Keep request handling in serving utilities. Move record_request_tools(), record_tool_call_response(), and record_tool_parser_invocation() into vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/tool_calls_utils.py. They inspect requests and update accumulators without exporting metrics. Keep the accumulator, Prometheus registration, and final exporter in the existing vllm/parser/metrics.py.
4. Share state through conversions. Attach private _tool_stats to request models, including native Anthropic and Cohere requests. Preserve identity through conversion to Chat requests and deep copies. Keep it outside public schemas and serialization. Capture supplied tool count before parser mutations. Remove _api_surface and its metrics special cases.
5. Use an explicit lifecycle boundary. Put track_tool_metrics() in tool_calls_utils.py, applied only to HTTP route handlers with (request, raw_request) -> Response. Export after ordinary response conversion and serialization, or after streaming iteration and generator cleanup. Keep serving methods and converters undecorated. Direct callers such as batch processing use an explicit tool_metrics_scope. Responses background tasks need a separate accumulator observed when their task finishes.
6. Record non-streaming outcomes provisionally. In chat_completion_full_generator(), retain counts and outcomes separately for each choice. Catch Anthropic argument-conversion failures around messages_full_converter() in create_messages(); keep the converter metrics-agnostic. Successful Anthropic and Cohere conversions preserve counts one-for-one, so avoid redundant recounting. Failed non-streaming responses emit zero calls, including when some choices were provisionally parsed successfully.
7. Count actual streaming emissions and completion per choice. Deduplicate (choice index, tool-call index) in the accumulator. Record Chat calls after serialization, immediately before yielding. Record Anthropic tool_use starts and Cohere tool-call-start events at their actual yield points, including when closing frames precede a new call. Track each choice’s completion independently: interrupted streams retain emitted counts, completed choices can retain their outcomes, and unfinished choices receive no completed outcome. Generic engine, serialization, and cancellation failures are not parsing failures. Close nested generators before final observation.
</details>
